meaning: A way to send messages using short and long signals, called dots and dashes, for letters and numbers.
clues: A way to send messages using only two kinds of signal, short and long.
Short and long taps, beeps, or flashes of light stand for letters and numbers.
It was made for the telegraph in the 1800s.
The distress call SOS is three short signals, three long ones, and three short.
It has two words. The first starts with M and is a person's last name.
assumes: Braille uses raised dots read by touch
Semaphore uses flags held in set positions
Sign language uses hand shapes and movement

decoys.meaning: A system of raised dots that people read by touch.
A way to send messages from far away by holding flags in set positions for each letter.
A language of hand shapes and movements, used by many deaf people.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: My cousin the telegraph was always chatting in dots and dashes. Dit dit dah!

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: a text message, sent in a second. Some radio hobbyists still use Morse code for fun.
